scenes.name: Crunk y trap en Atlanta
scenes.book: The Come Up: An Oral History of the Rise of Hip-Hop
scenes.desc: Lil Jon, A&R de So So Def, se convirtió con los East Side Boyz en la cara del crunk (Get Crunk, Who U Wit, 1997). En 1999 Def Jam ya no pudo ignorar el Sur y creó Def Jam South con Scarface al frente, que fichó a Chris Lova Lova, DJ de Hot 97.5 que vendía Incognegro desde el maletero: Ludacris (Back for the First Time, 2000). T.I., tras fracasar en Arista, se hizo fuerte con las mixtapes de DJ Drama, fundó Grand Hustle y con Trap Muzik (2003) llevó al gran público el trap, la música de la calle del trapicheo: sintetizadores, baterías potentes y charles nerviosos, con productores como DJ Toomp, Shawty Redd, Drumma Boy, Lex Luger o Zaytoven, cuyo piano hizo brillar a Gucci Mane (en un solo día de 2009 salieron «Bricks» y «Make Tha Trap Say Aye»). Luego Jeezy, Future, Migos, 21 Savage o Lil Baby: Atlanta, ciudad del fénix, destruye su sonido cada pocos años para crear otro.

scenes.name: El fin del sampleo libre y el oficio del productor
scenes.book: The Come Up: An Oral History of the Rise of Hip-Hop
scenes.desc: Transformar lo que existía en algo nuevo está en la base del hip hop: de los breaks de los pioneros a la caja de Marley Marl, el muro de la Bomb Squad y los collages de jazz de De La Soul, Tribe, Pete Rock o DJ Premier. Nadie pensaba en derechos hasta que el rap dio dinero. En diciembre de 1991 Gilbert O’Sullivan ganó a Biz Markie por samplear «Alone Again (Naturally)» sin permiso (250.000 dólares y la retirada del disco); De La Soul pactó con los Turtles. Biz llamó a su siguiente disco All Samples Cleared! y el salvaje Oeste se acabó: a los productores de Rush les dieron una lista de artistas intocables, y Easy Mo Bee empezó a samplear instrumentos sueltos y tocar encima («Flava in Ya Ear»). «La cultura negra siempre recibe las sobras y las convierte en lo que lo controla todo» (Salaam Remi). El productor es también psiquiatra y entrenador; hoy se hace un éxito con un portátil, y algunos, como Timbaland regalándole su archivo de sonidos a Just Blaze, rompieron la costumbre de tapar las etiquetas.

scenes.name: Grammys, Óscars, Hall of Fame y el Pulitzer
scenes.book: The Come Up: An Oral History of the Rise of Hip-Hop
scenes.desc: Los grandes premios rechazaron o reconocieron tarde al hip hop. En los Grammy de 1984, la noche de Thriller, Herbie Hancock tocó «Rockit» con Grand Mixer D.ST en los platos: para Paradise Gray, la primera vez que se vio en la tele. En 1989 se creó el Grammy al mejor rap pero se entregó fuera de la retransmisión: Def Jam y Rush encabezaron el boicot y DJ Jazzy Jeff & the Fresh Prince no fueron a recoger el premio por «Parents Just Don’t Understand»; Kool Moe Dee sí fue, harto de que nadie hablara de estrategia («¿no decíamos que nos importaba un carajo el Grammy?»). En 1990 Young MC lo ganó en directo a «Fight the Power» y Flavor Flav le asaltó el escenario. Eminem fue el primer rapero en ganar un Óscar con «Lose Yourself» (2003, con Luis Resto), y Three 6 Mafia el segundo; Grandmaster Flash and the Furious Five entraron los primeros en el Rock and Roll Hall of Fame (2007). En 2014 Macklemore se disculpó con Kendrick Lamar por ganarle; en 2018 DAMN. de Lamar, criado en Top Dawg por Punch, ganó el Pulitzer, algo que Nation of Millions habría merecido treinta años antes.

scenes.name: Escribir rimas: libretas, cabezas y negros
scenes.book: The Come Up: An Oral History of the Rise of Hip-Hop
scenes.desc: Desde Rakim, KRS-One y Kane, la lírica es un arte competitivo: unos escriben en libretas, otros en el móvil en un atasco, otros, como Biggie, Jay-Z o Styles P, en la cabeza. Para unos hay que «dejar joyas» y enseñar (Chuck D: «no rimo por rimar»); para otros basta con que suene bien sobre la base. Cormega tira nueve de cada diez rimas; K-Rino dice que el bloqueo es falta de lecturas; Bruce Lee y las diez mil horas. El negro (ghostwriting) existe desde que Caz rapeó sin saberlo en «Rapper’s Delight»: Kane escribía para la Juice Crew, The D.O.C. y Eminem para Dr. Dre, y Meek Mill acusó a Drake; para unos traiciona la autenticidad, para otros es como Al Pacino haciendo de cubano.

scenes.name: El hip hop: medio siglo de historia oral
scenes.book: The Come Up: An Oral History of the Rise of Hip-Hop
scenes.desc: Un género nacido de la imaginación de chavales abandonados entre las ruinas del Bronx de los setenta que sobrevivió a todo (a una generación mayor que lo rechazaba, a las radios que no lo ponían, a los políticos que lo atacaban) hasta convertirse en la música más popular de Estados Unidos. Abrams hizo más de trescientas entrevistas entre 2018 y 2022 a DJs, artistas, productores, ejecutivos y periodistas para contar su origen y su expansión: del Bronx a los demás distritos «como las venas de un plano del metro», del parque al vinilo, a la Costa Oeste con el gangsta rap y el G-funk, al Sur y más allá. «La lírica es, al fin y al cabo, una forma de tradición oral.»

facts.title: COVID-19 Pandemic and Songwriting (2020)
facts.body: The COVID-19 pandemic provided an unexpected opportunity for the band, with nothing to do but write songs. They wrote constantly from January to October 2020, resulting in over a hundred songs for their new album. "Writing a new album started almost immediately...They wrote constantly from January to October 2020 as COVID raged all around them. As Anthony said, with the pandemic, there was nothing to do but write songs."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

facts.title: Publishing Rights Sale to Eldridge Industries (Prior to 2020)
facts.body: The Killers sold the publishing rights to all their songs created from their formation until 2020 to Eldridge Industries, a company that invests in various sectors including insurance, real estate, and music. The exact price was not revealed, but it is speculated to be in excess of $100 million due to the enduring popularity and high streaming numbers of their music. This lump sum payment offers tax advantages, being treated as a capital gain rather than income, and provides financial security for the band, allowing them to continue making new music and touring while Eldridge focuses on maximizing catalog revenue. "Eldridge Industries and they invested everything from insurance to real estate to music. So how much did they pay the killers for all those songs released prior to 2020? No idea because the price was never revealed."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

facts.title: HBO Documentary: How Can You Mend a Broken Heart (2020)
facts.body: HBO released a new documentary titled "The Bee Gees, How Can You Mend a Broken Heart," directed by Frank Marshall. The film chronicles the highs and lows of brothers Barry, Maurice, and Robin Gibb, exploring the evolution of their prolific career, their navigation of the ever-changing music industry, and the complex dynamics of family and fame through interviews and never-before-seen footage. "HBO's new documentary The Bee Gees, how can you mend a broken heart? Chronicles the highs and lows of brothers Barry, Morris and Robin Gibb in the evolution of their prolific career as The Bee Gees."
facts.source: For the Record - The 70s

facts.title: Grammy Win for "No Time to Die" Amidst Film Delays (2020)
facts.body: Billie Eilish's theme song for "No Time to Die" was released in February 2020, intended to align with an early movie release date. However, the film suffered multiple postponements due to COVID-19, leaving the song without its accompanying film for 18 months. Despite this unusual circumstance, the song still managed to win a Grammy Award for Best Song, Written for Visual Media. "Meanwhile, though, it somehow managed to win a Grammy award for Best Song, Written for Visual Media."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Billie Eilish

facts.title: Tom Meighan Dismissed July 2020 After Assault Conviction; Serge Pizzorno New Frontman from October 2021
facts.body: Kasabian formed in 1997 and carved out a successful career in the UK over more than a decade. In July 2020, founding singer and member Tom Meighan announced he was leaving — a mutual decision following his admission in court that he had assaulted his ex-fiancée in front of their child, which was a clear red line for the rest of the band. facts.title: Youngest Bond Theme Artist
facts.body: Billie Eilish, along with her brother Finneas O'Connell, wrote and recorded the theme song for the James Bond film "No Time to Die" over three days on a tour bus in late 2019. It was recorded in England with a 70-piece orchestra. The song was released on February 13, 2020, to coincide with a postponed movie release, but the film faced further delays due to COVID-19, leaving the song without a concurrent film for 18 months. Eilish was 18 at the time, making her the youngest person ever to record a Bond theme. The song later won a Grammy Award for Best Song, Written for Visual Media. "She and Brother Finneas wrote and recorded it over three days on a tour bus in late 2019."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: No Time to Die

It was previewed by a recording of "Patience" (originally by Guns N' Roses), released on July 20, 2020 — what would have been Chris's 56th birthday. Released during the depths of the pandemic, the album largely flew under the radar. "If that record escaped your attention, you're forgiven. We had other things going on."

facts.title: Scottish Bars Implement Low Volume Rule (2020)
facts.body: In 2020, Scottish bars implemented a rule to keep the volume low on all music and televisions. This measure was intended to prevent people from having to shout over noise, which authorities believed would help control the spread of COVID-19. "The volume had to be kept low on all music and all televisions so people wouldn't have to shout over the noise."

facts.body: HBO released a 2020 documentary titled "Showbiz Kids," which featured interviews with various former child stars, including Will Wheaton, Henry Thomas, and Todd Bridges, and had a soundtrack composed by Jeff Tweedy and his sons Spencer and Sam. facts.title: Polyvinyl Chloride (PVC) Shortage (2020 onwards)
facts.body: A global shortage of polyvinyl chloride (PVC) began in 2020, primarily due to supply chain disruptions caused by the pandemic. While increased online record sales and backed-up pressing plants contributed, a major factor in the shortage was the surging demand for plastic containers used by take-out restaurants. "Starting in 2020, the world suffered a shortage of polyvinyl chloride because of supply chain issues during the pandemic."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

facts.title: 2020 Impact on Touring Industry
facts.body: The touring industry faced an "apocalyptic" year in 2020, suffering an estimated $30 billion USD loss due to a lack of gigs and revenues. This led to many musicians being unemployed or driving Uber, no work for roadies, and sound and light companies losing business, with venues shutting down or closing entirely and festivals being cancelled. "It has been a Pocca Liptic for the touring industry. No gigs, no revenues, live music industry probably lost $30 billion US dollars this year."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

facts.title: Christmas Song for Dogs (2020)
facts.body: A Christmas song specifically for dogs was created in the UK in 2020 by a vet and a dog behavioralist. Recorded at Abbey Road, it incorporates sounds dogs enjoy, such as squeaky toys, bells, and "arphats," and is set to a reggae beat, aiming to reduce stress. Sales proceeds go to an animal charity. "Taking all this research and more into account, we now have a Christmas song for dogs in 2020."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

facts.title: Record Store Day Scheduling and 2020 Changes
facts.body: Record Store Day is typically held on the third Saturday of April, with a secondary event scheduled for Black Friday in November. In 2020, due to the COVID-19 pandemic, the schedule was adjusted to include three Record Store Days in addition to the Black Friday sale. "Normally, record store day is held on the third Saturday of April with a secondary event scheduled for Black Friday in November."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The History of the Record Store

facts.title: COVID-19 Pandemic as Creative Catalyst (2020)
facts.body: The pandemic, by limiting other activities, provided an environment where the Red Hot Chili Peppers could focus intensely on songwriting, leading to over a hundred new songs for "Unlimited Love." "They wrote constantly from January to October 2020 as COVID raged all around them. As Anthony said, with the pandemic, there was nothing to do but write songs."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The Long Strange Trip of John Frusciante Part 2

facts.title: Vinyl Sales Exceeding CDs (2020)
facts.body: In 2020, the dollar value of vinyl sold in the United States surpassed that of CDs for the first time since 1986, indicating a significant financial turnaround and profitability for the vinyl format. "It got to the point that in 2020, the dollar value of vinyl sold exceeded that of CDs in the United States. That hadn't happened since 1986."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
